00374.title: Trabectedin for advanced soft tissue sarcoma: treatment and checks
00374.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00374.setting: Adult advanced soft tissue sarcoma after anthracycline and ifosfamide treatment has failed, or when those medicines are unsuitable
00374.summary: Trabectedin 1.5 mg/m² is infused over 24 hours starting on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Treatment continues while benefit and tolerability justify it. The actual dose, start time and any delay require a new safety review.

milestones.title: Treatment review
milestones.why: The aim is to control advanced sarcoma and help symptoms. The strongest trial evidence concerns previously treated liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma; the team explains expected benefit for your particular subtype.
milestones.clinical: Trabectedin 1.5 mg/m² is infused over 24 hours starting on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Treatment continues while benefit and tolerability justify it. The actual dose, start time and any delay require a new safety review.
milestones.action: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999. Marked muscle pain or weakness, dark or reduced urine, new swelling or faintness, jaundice, breathlessness or infusion-site pain requires urgent assessment.

00462.title: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin for Kaposi sarcoma: treatment and checks
00462.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00462.setting: acquired immunodeficiency syndrome-related Kaposi sarcoma with a CD4 helper T-cell (infection-fighting immune-cell) count below 200 cells/mm³ and extensive disease of skin or mucous membranes, or internal organs
00462.summary: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m² is given on day 1 every 21 days. National Cancer Control Programme specifies a maximum of 6 cycles or earlier stopping for progression or unacceptable toxicity. A 14-day interval is a separately selected alternative and must be written into the personal prescription.

00554.summary: Vinblastine 6 mg/m² and methotrexate 30 mg/m² are given on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Day 22 is a planned break. National Cancer Control Programme describes 12 cycles unless progression or unacceptable toxicity requires a change.

milestones.title: Treatment review
milestones.when: Vinblastine and methotrexate on days 1, 8 and 15; repeat every 28 days
milestones.why: Desmoid tumours do not spread to distant organs but can grow locally, cause pain and impair function. This treatment aims to control troublesome or progressive local disease and preserve daily function; it is not a metastatic-cancer survival treatment.
milestones.clinical: Vinblastine 6 mg/m² and methotrexate 30 mg/m² are given on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Day 22 is a planned break. National Cancer Control Programme describes 12 cycles unless progression or unacceptable toxicity requires a change.
milestones.action: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999. New dry cough or breathlessness, severe mouth ulcers or diarrhoea, reduced urine, jaundice, or painful constipation with vomiting or abdominal swelling requires urgent advice.
